issues.description: Method visibility mismatch for Animal.messageOnFeed(): The problem statement UML (problem_statement.md) declares Animal.messageOnFeed() as a public abstract method (UML shows a plus-sign and {abstract} on the method). The solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) declares the method as protected: 'protected abstract String messageOnFeed();'. This difference can confuse students about which access modifier to use when implementing subclasses and may cause unexpected compilation or access issues if they follow the UML but the reference uses protected.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent. Preferably change the solution signature to 'public abstract String messageOnFeed();' in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java to match the UML and problem statement. Alternatively, update the UML/problem text to explicitly state 'protected' if protected was intended. Document the chosen visibility in the problem text so students implement subclasses with the correct access level.
